abstract: We prove $S_{3/10,3/10,3/10}(X)\ll_\varepsilon X^{23/43+\varepsilon}$ for the number of primitive positive integer solutions to $a+b=c\leq X$ satisfying $\text{rad}(a)\leq a^{3/10}$, $\text{rad}(b)\leq b^{3/10}$, and $\text{rad}(c)\leq c^{3/10}$. This improves both the total-budget collision exponent $71/130$ of [7] (by $63/5590$) and the refined total-budget exponent $677/1240$ of [8] (by $591/53320$). More generally, we replace the single combined radical budget in the exponent linear program of Bernert, Browning, Lichtman and Teräväinen [3] by three independent coordinate budgets $\rho=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in(0,1]^3$ and incorporate the empty-third-modulus collision inequalities of [7]. Exact rational branch certificates and attaining rational points determine the exact optima of both the Fourier-and-geometry relaxation $\mathcal P_0(\rho)$ and the collision-augmented relaxation $\mathcal P_{\text{ss0}}(\rho)$ across a benchmark parameter grid, separating the saving due to independent budgets from the saving contributed by collision constraints. Replaying the leaf multipliers yields a certified three-parameter piecewise affine upper envelope $E(\rho)$, illustrated along the diagonal slice $\rho=(u,u,u)$ in the supplement. All optimization equalities concern the specified finite-dimensional relaxations; attaining points do not provide lower bounds for the arithmetic counting function.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Updated reference [7] to identify the published rStation version math_17 v2 (alongside v1) and updated reference [8] to give its published rStation identifier math_28 v2 (alongside v1).
- Labeled the comparison column of the Theorem 6.1 grid table and supplement tables explicitly as `[7]-based baseline`, and explained in Sections 1 and 6 that at (1/3,1/3,1/3) (t=1), D_{ss0}(1/3,1/3,1/3)=283/477 improves the [7]-based baseline 5588/9417 by 155/1497303 = 465/4491909 while [8, Theorem 1.2] already gives 589903/1000008 < 283/477 via S_rho <= N_1, whereas at (3/10,3/10,3/10) (t=9/10), the separate-budget exponent 23/43 strictly improves both 71/130 of [7] (by 63/5590) and 677/1240 of [8] (by 591/53320).
- Added Figure 1 (`supplement/figure-1.png`) and `plot_diagonal_slice.py` plotting the pure separate-budget tree envelopes E_0(u,u,u) and E(u,u,u) (reaching 12/11 at u=2/3) and exact diagonal grid optima D_0(u,u,u) and D_{ss0}(u,u,u) (12/11 at u=2/3) alongside the explicit literature bound of [1]-[3] (including 3/5 for 3u<1 with an open endpoint at u=1/3), the [7]-based baseline, and the total-budget values of [8], while keeping verify_release.py pure Python standard library.
- Replaced all assert statements in supplement verification scripts with explicit ValueError checks so verification runs identically under python3 -O, translated Chinese comments in summarize.py to English, unified notation P_{ss0} and citation [1] in Sections 6-7, streamlined the author header to the standard affiliation line, and expanded the abstract from 127 to 166 words.
title: Separated radical budgets for the Mazur–Kane counting problem
